question: Which Gupta ruler was known for defeating the Sakas in western regions, assuming the title of "Vikramaditya'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta - II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta II

 
 
• One of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta II, also known by his given name Vikramaditya and Chandragupta Vikramaditya.
 
• He was the third ruler of the Gupta Empire in India.
 
• The famous Chandragupta II was the child of Samudragupta and Datta Devi.
 
• The Gupta empire was extended by Chandragupta II to the western sea coast, a vital area for trade and commerce.
 
• As a result, Malwa and Ujjain (Ujjayini), the region's capital, enjoyed prosperity.
 
• The second capital of Chandragupta II was Ujjayini.

Gupta Dynasty:

 
 
 

 Gupta Dynasty Kings
 Facts about Gupta Kings
 
 

 Sri Gupta
 
 
 
• Founder of Gupta Dynasty
 
• Reign from 240 CE to 280 CE
 
• Used the title of ‘Maharaja‘
 
 
 
 

 Ghatotkacha
 
 
 
• Son of Sri Gupta
 
• Took the title of ‘Maharaja‘
 
 
 
 

 Chandragupta I
 
 
 
• Reigned from 319 CE to 335/336 CE
 
• Started the Gupta Era
 
• He assumed the title of ‘Maharajadhiraja‘
 
• Married Lichchavi princess Kumaradevi
 
 
 
 

 Samudragupta
 
 
 
• Reigned from 335/336 CE to 375 CE
 
• Called ‘Napolean of India’ by V.A. Smith (Irish Indologist and Art Historian)
 
• His campaigns are mentioned in the Eran inscription (Madhya Pradesh)
 
 
 
 

 Chandragupta II
 
 
 
• Reigned from 376-413/415 CE
 
• Navratnas (9 Gems in his Court)
 
• Took the title ‘Vikramaditya’
 
 
 
 

 Kumaragupta I
 
 
 
• Reigned from 415 CE to 455 CE
 
• Founded Nalanda University
 
• He was also called Shakraditya
 
 
 
 

 Skandagupta
 
 
 
• Reigned from 455 AD – 467 AD
 
• Was a ‘Vaishnavite‘
 
• Son of Kumaragupta
 
• Repulsed an attack by the Hunas but this strained his empire’s coffers
 
 
 
 

 Vishnugupta
 
 
 
• Last known ruler of the Gupta Dynasty (540 AD – 550 AD)
